author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Indigenous West Papuans have taken to the streets across Indonesia’s resource-rich West Papua region to mark the 64th anniversary of the signing of the New York Agreement.

In Jayapura and other towns, demonstrators were met with tear gas and water cannon fired by Indonesian police. The 1962 agreement transferred control of the former Dutch colony to the United Nations and later to Indonesia, ending hopes of independence for many Indigenous West Papuans.

Civil society groups, including the West Papua National Committee, say the denial of self-determination remains a root cause of the decades-long conflict.

Military operations in the region have forced tens of thousands of people from their homes, while Jakarta has deployed large numbers of troops. The Indonesian government maintains that West Papua is part of its sovereign territory and continues to reject independence efforts.

Al Jazeera’s Joel Evans reports.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Parts of Europe are battling widespread wildfires after weeks of intense heat and bone-dry conditions.

Croatia is fighting some of its worst fires in years, with military aircraft helping hundreds of firefighters battle blazes near the coast. On the Pelješac Peninsula, residents have been forced from their homes and livelihoods destroyed.

Montenegro is also facing several active wildfires, while Spain has been overwhelmed by fires for weeks. In France, firefighters are using tactical burns to slow the spread of flames by removing fuel ahead of advancing fire fronts.

In England, fires have destroyed homes across parts of the Midlands, forcing hundreds of people to evacuate. An emergency alert was issued across England and Wales warning of the risk of fires.

The prolonged heat is putting pressure on infrastructure across Europe, much of which was not designed to withstand temperatures increasingly fuelled by climate change.

Al Jazeera’s Frances Read reports from London.

title: Europe battles wildfires as extreme heat fuels blazes across the continent

description:
An ongoing drought in the Netherlands is threatening the dykes that protect densely populated areas from flooding. Cracks are appearing across the region, raising concerns among water authorities.

To protect water levels and maintain water safety, authorities have banned the use of fresh water from dykes for irrigation and imposed heavy fines. 

The measures have caused panic in Westland, home to the world’s largest greenhouse industry, where hundreds of growers risk losing vegetables and flowers if they cannot secure enough water.

Water authorities have collected fresh water as a backup, but warn that supplies could also run dry if the drought continues. More drastic measures, including the possible use of treated sewage water, may be needed.

Al Jazeera’s Step Vaessen reports near The Hague.

description:

US Attorney for New York's Southern District Jamie McDonald pushed back on any justification, saying "no grievance, political belief, or ideological cause can ever justify murder. There can be no celebrity in assassination." The case has fuelled debate over inequalities in US healthcare, where 28 million people can't afford or can't get insurance. Mangione returns to court on December 18 for sentencing, facing 25 to 30 years, while his lawyer, Karen Friedman Agnifilo, says he's been "unfairly treated... in every way" as he fights a separate state murder charge the Manhattan District Attorney wants to bring to trial in September, arguing double jeopardy protections don't apply. 

Al Jazeera's Richard Gaisford reports from New York.

The governor of the US state of Indiana has declared an emergency after storms pounded parts of the Midwest, cutting power to hundreds of thousands of homes as emergency crews worked to rescue residents from flash flooding. 

Powerful thunderstorms known as derechos produced wind gusts of 160km/h, and tornadoes tore through parts of the Chicago area, damaging homes and knocking out power to more than 300,000 people across three states. Forecasters are predicting additional rainfall as the region braces for more bad weather in the coming days.
